record.paper_title: Some open problems in control theory.
record.context_brief: periodic stabilization in dimensions two or three
record.original_question: In dimensions 2 and 3, suppose a control system satisfies small-time reachability together with a Lie algebra condition. Do these hypotheses imply the existence of a periodic stabilizing feedback or periodic stabilization mechanism? The source states that positive answers are already known in the other dimensions from the author's work.

evidence.quote: 2) Does small time reachability (and a Lie algebra condition) imply periodic stabilization in dimension two or three? (the other dimensions provide positive answers due to the work of the author);

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a smooth control-affine system on $\mathbb{R}^n$ of the form
$$\dot x = f(x,u), \qquad x \in \mathbb{R}^n,\ u \in \mathbb{R}^m,$$
with $f$ smooth and $f(0,0)=0$. Recall:

(a) The system is small-time locally controllable at $(0,0)$ if for every $T>0$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\eta>0$ such that for every $x_0,x_1\in\mathbb{R}^n$ with $|x_0|+|x_1|\le\eta$, there is a measurable control $u:[0,T]\to\mathbb{R}^m$ with $\|u\|_\infty\le\varepsilon$ steering the state from $x_0$ at time $0$ to $x_1$ at time $T$.

(b) The system satisfies the Lie algebra rank condition at $0$ if the Lie algebra generated by the vector fields $x\mapsto f(x,u)$, $u\in\mathbb{R}^m$, evaluated at $0$, equals $\mathbb{R}^n$.

(c) The origin is locally asymptotically stabilizable by means of periodic time-varying feedback if there exist $T>0$ and a continuous map $u:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^m$ with $u(0,t)=0$ and $u(x,t+T)=u(x,t)$ for all $(x,t)$, such that $0$ is a locally asymptotically stable equilibrium of the closed-loop system $\dot x = f(x,u(x,t))$.

For $n\in\{4,5,6,\dots\}$ it is known that (a) and (b) together imply (c). Question: does the same implication hold when $n=2$ or $n=3$? That is, in dimensions two and three, does small-time local controllability together with the Lie algebra rank condition at $0$ imply local asymptotic stabilizability of $0$ by means of a continuous periodic time-varying feedback law?
artifact.category_tag: Periodic stabilization of nonlinear control systems
artifact.status_search_result: The implication from small-time local controllability (with the Lie algebra rank condition) to local asymptotic stabilizability by continuous periodic time-varying feedback is established for state-space dimensions $n\ge 4$ (Coron). The cases $n=2,3$ remain singled out as open problems in Coron's overview of his main works in control theory; no resolution in dimensions two or three has been located in subsequent literature.

status_evidence.title: My main works in control theory
status_evidence.snippet: Result giving asymptotic stabilization by periodic time-varying feedback for small-time locally controllable systems when the dimension of the state is not 2 or 3.
status_evidence.claim: The positive result for dimensions other than 2 and 3 is attributed to Coron, with dimensions 2 and 3 noted as remaining cases.

status_evidence.title: On the Stabilization in Finite Time of Locally Controllable Systems by Means of Continuous Time-Varying Feedback Law
status_evidence.snippet: Stabilization by continuous periodic time-varying feedback laws under controllability and rank-type assumptions, with conditions on the dimension of the state space.
status_evidence.claim: The general theorem on periodic time-varying stabilization is proved under dimensional restrictions excluding low dimensions.
